---
title: "019 — Security posture detection"
---

> **Status:** standing (one leg degraded: platform push protection was verified
> non-enforcing on this repo; the enforcement gap is a recorded follow-up, not
> a fix in this feature)

**Goal.** Make the project automatically tell the maintainer when dependencies,
release artifacts, or committed content introduce known weaknesses. Detection
latency was previously infinite — only manual audits surfaced anything — and
the freshly public launch ([017 — secure public
launch](017-secure-public-launch.qmd)) made that gap consequential. The
assessment's verdict was Option B: zero-config detection, strictly report-only.

**Why.** Posture was maintained by hand and memory while the product went
internet-facing. Report-only was a deliberate ruling, not a compromise: a solo
maintainer's noise budget, plus the constraint that security work must never tax
features, performance, or the one-step install. Everything runs upstream of the
shipped artifact; artifact hardening (digest pinning, non-root containers, TLS
defaults) was explicitly out of scope, as was gating any merge or release on
findings.

**Outcome & reversals.** Merged as PR #27 (2026-09-05); the entire diff is two
workflow files and repo settings, nothing under `src/` or `server/`.
Dependabot vulnerability alerts and security updates went live via settings
alone — no `dependabot.yml`, because scheduled version-update floods were
explicitly declined against the noise budget — and enablement immediately
surfaced 40 known vulnerabilities on the default branch, converting detection
latency from never to same-day. A report-only CI job audits all three manifest
roots on every PR, and each release leg Trivy-scans its built image into job
summaries, per-image SARIF categories, and artifacts, with explicit
clean/findings/scan-failed lines so a scan that did not run can never masquerade
as a clean result. Rehearsal proved the surface carries real signal: the server
image held CRITICAL and HIGH CVEs while the web image scanned clean. The
reversal of expectation came in US3, which assumed push protection was already
live and merely needed proving: live tests (re-run two days later to rule out
propagation lag) showed AWS-pattern enforcement never engages on this
personal-account public repo despite settings reporting enabled — pushes of
synthetic credentials sailed through with zero alerts. The owner accepted a
degraded US3 (2026-09-05), recorded FR-005/FR-006 as unmet by the platform, and
spun the enforcement gap out as a follow-up rather than scope-creeping a
compensating scanner into a report-only feature. The first Dependabot security
PR's release-contract check stays open as an event-driven task.

**Learnings.**

- "Enabled" in a settings API is not "enforcing" — a verification-only story
  still needs a live adversarial test, and the test was the feature.
- Report-only is a design: never-gate plus never-silence delivers signal
  without creating a new way to block a release.
- Zero-config beats config: continuous dependency-graph alerts removed
  detection latency without adding one scheduled task to maintain.
- The shipped artifact deserves its own per-release record — image scans see
  the full OS-plus-application closure a lockfile audit cannot.
- Accepting a degraded outcome with a recorded follow-up beats bending a
  report-only feature to absorb a compensating tool.
